summary:
Directly addressing NASA’s Exploration Medical Capability (ExMC) gap Medical-701 and Level of Care IV/V guidelines (HRP-48033), we developed CrewSignal: an autonomous, 100% offline Clinical Decision Support System (CDSS) for deep-space exploration.

  During long-duration Mars transit, 22-minute communication delays render real-time Mission Control assistance impossible, while strict spacecraft constraints prohibit cloud services or internet access. CrewSignal fulfills NASA’s Concept of Operations by providing an on-station medical edge hub that ingests
  live 1 Hz multi-channel wearable telemetry—including heart rate with physiological heart rate variability (HRV), arterial pressure, core-skin temperature, and actigraphy—running entirely locally on standard habitat computing hardware.

  Calibrated against authentic NASA Life Sciences Data Archive (LSDA) datasets from the 45-day HERA isolation mission and ISS microgravity protocols, CrewSignal features dynamic clinical reference gauges, custom telemetry imports, and an on-device emergency voice triage assistant with hardware silence controls
  for low-visibility or crew incapacitation crises. A dual-tier privacy firewall protects astronaut psychological reporting from mission telemetry.

  CrewSignal is vital because, per NASA HRP-48033, autonomous on-board decision support is the only way to safeguard crew health, manage emergent crises, and ensure mission survival beyond low-Earth orbit.
details:
1. What does it do and how does it work?

CrewSignal is an autonomous, 100% offline Clinical Decision Support System (CDSS) and health-monitoring platform designed for long-duration spaceflight. Built strictly to address NASA’s Exploration Medical Capability (ExMC) gap Medical-701 and Level of Care IV/V standards (NASA-STD-3001 & HRP-48033),

CrewSignal enables non-physician crew members to independently monitor daily vitals, track longitudinal physiological trends, and execute immediate clinical triage during communications blackouts.

The system operates across three synchronized tiers:

1. Multi-Channel Ingestion & IoT Hardware Abstraction Layer: CrewSignal is architected to ingest live serial and Web Bluetooth streams from low-voltage wearable bench nodes:

• MAX30102 Optical PPG Sensor: Captures real-time pulse rate and optical waveforms with signal-quality gating.

• Infrared (IR) Contact Thermistor (MAX30205 / MLX90614): Tracks non-contact skin-surface thermal dissipation and metabolic warming.

• MPU6050 3-Axis IMU: Measures acceleration and actigraphy to categorize microgravity float (0.02–0.08 g), station duty (0.20–0.55 g), and high-load countermeasure workouts (0.90–1.75 g).

• Validated Flight Emulation & Telemetry Importer: When physical sensors are unstrapped, CrewSignal executes a 1 Hz flight emulation engine driven by real NASA Life Sciences Data Archive (LSDA) missions, complete with Respiratory Sinus Arrhythmia (RSA) and Mayer baroreflex oscillations, while allowing

flight surgeons to drag and drop custom mission CSV/JSON datasets.

2. Interactive Clinical Dashboard & Body Map: Translates complex telemetry into an interactive SVG body map. Rather than showing arbitrary clamp limits, gauges display NASA Standard Clinical Reference Scales (e.g. 45–180 bpm for Heart Rate, with nominal resting bands highlighted at 70–100 bpm),

contextualized by recent 60-second rolling spans.

3. Hands-Free Emergency Protocol Engine: In low-visibility or crew incapacitation scenarios (such as exercise-induced tachycardia), a single prominent trigger activates on-device auditory clinical triage (pickAdamVoice profile) with instant hardware physical "Stop Speaker" controls.

4. Dual-Tier Astronaut Privacy Firewall: Differentiates between physical vitals (shared for mission safety) and self-reported mental wellbeing/stress check-ins, which remain encrypted locally to eliminate astronaut under-reporting fear.

2. What benefits does it have?

• Zero Cloud & Zero Network Dependency: Operates reliably inside an RF-shielded spacecraft Faraday cage or deep-space transit without internet or external APIs.

• Honest Data Quality Gate: Unlike commercial apps that display misleading zeros or mask missing data as green, CrewSignal tags every reading with quality flags (ok, poor_contact, stale). If sensor contact fails, it prominently displays "No valid reading."

• Emergency Speed: Emergency workflows never wait for data entry or sensor handshake—immediate guided checklists open on a single click.

• Asynchronous Earth Telemetry Bundler: Automatically packages structured JSON clinical handoff reports ready for delay-tolerant satellite downlink once ground communication windows open.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

As human spaceflight ventures beyond Low Earth Orbit (LEO) toward Mars, real-time medical evacuation is impossible. CrewSignal shifts space medicine from an Earth-dependent paradigm to on-station medical autonomy. Beyond spaceflight, its zero-bandwidth, offline-first design provides immediate humanitarian

impact for remote polar stations, offshore marine vessels, and underserved rural clinics cut off from internet infrastructure.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

• Frontend Framework: Next.js 16 (App Router), React 19, TypeScript

• State & Storage Architecture: Service Worker Cache (PRECACHE_SHELL), HTML5 PWA Manifest, LocalStorage Indexed Persistence

• Visualization & UI: Tailwind CSS, Custom Aerospace Vector Design System, Dynamic SVG Body Map, HTML5 Particle Engine

• Voice & Speech Engine: Built-in offline Web Speech Synthesis API tuned to mission-commander acoustics with immediate audio pause/stop interrupt handlers

• IoT & Sensor Hardware Research: MAX30102 (PPG optical pulse), MPU6050 (3-axis IMU actigraphy), IR temperature module (contact skin thermistor), ESP32 development microcontrollers

• Data Ingestion: Custom client-side streaming CSV/JSON parser with validation preview and schema verification

5. How is your project creative?

• The "Honest Uncertainty" Design Philosophy: Rather than inventing an unverified medical diagnosis or artificial "health score," CrewSignal focuses on clinical observation, verified procedural checklists, and transparent data quality.

• Acoustic Emergency Co-Pilot: The voice engine speaks procedural instructions aloud, allowing a second astronaut to perform CPR or retrieve an AED without taking their eyes off the patient.

• Behavioral Privacy Separation: Solving the historical dilemma where astronauts hide psychological distress by guaranteeing that mental health logs stay strictly private on the local vessel.

6. What factors did your team consider?

• NASA Exploration Constraints (HRP-48033 Section 4.5): Strict mass, power (70 W), and low-compute laptop environments with zero cloud connectivity.

• Sensor Motion Artifacts: Microgravity movement causes PPG sensor detachment; CrewSignal accounts for contact noise and motion clipping rather than outputting false cardiac alarms.

• Cognitive Overload: In high-stress scenarios, complex menus cause deadly delays; the emergency flow is restricted to high-contrast, one-instruction-per-screen guidance.
